scorecard.claim_text: The ancient Egyptian pyramids at Giza were constructed using concrete poured into molds rather than by assembling quarried stone blocks.
The first photograph of a black hole, released by the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration in 2019, was an optical photograph taken by a single telescope operating at visible wavelengths.

In the Epic of Gilgamesh, a surviving text depicts a flood survivor who builds a vessel, preserves living creatures, and survives a catastrophic flood, but the existence of this literary account does not by itself establish that a supernatural flood occurred in the objective historical world.
The Moon landing conspiracy narrative is false, and the presence of retroreflectors placed on the lunar surface by Apollo missions allows laser ranging experiments to measure the Earth-Moon distance.
A scientific paper's appearance in a peer-reviewed journal guarantees that every factual assertion in the paper is true and that its results can never be overturned by later evidence.

In the Book of Exodus, Moses is described as leading the Israelites out of Egypt, but the literary account alone does not establish every detail of the event as an independently verified archaeological fact.

The existence of a manuscript containing a prediction of a future event establishes that the event was supernaturally revealed before it happened, regardless of when the manuscript was composed or whether its dating is secure.

The BB84 protocol was published in 1984, Stephen Wiesner's conjugate-coding manuscript was published in 1983, and therefore the published Wiesner manuscript was the source from which Bennett and Brassard copied the complete BB84 protocol in 1984.

Because the Michelson-Morley experiment failed to detect the expected classical ether wind, it proved that the speed of light is invariant in every inertial frame and that special relativity follows logically from that experiment alone.

The 1919 solar-eclipse observations supported Einstein's prediction of gravitational light deflection, and because those observations were later scrutinized, general relativity has never received any independent experimental confirmation.

A manuscript dated to the second century BCE contains a prophecy that resembles an event from the first century BCE; this chronological ordering alone proves the prophecy was supernaturally revealed before the event, even if the manuscript's date and textual history are uncertain.

Since the Great Isaiah Scroll is substantially older than the medieval Masoretic codices, every word in every modern translation of Isaiah has been demonstrated to match the wording of the second-century-BCE manuscript exactly.

The discovery of a fossil with an anatomically modern feature proves that the individual belonged to a fully modern human population, even if the fossil's age, surrounding fossils, and evolutionary context remain disputed.

A paper published in a peer-reviewed journal reports a statistically significant association between two variables; therefore, the first variable caused the second, the association must replicate in every population, and no confounding variable can explain the result.

A historical source explicitly states that a ruler ordered a temple to be built, and an inscription independently confirms that the temple existed; these two facts alone establish that the surviving temple foundations were constructed entirely during that ruler's reign and were never rebuilt or modified.

If a quantum measurement produces one outcome with probability one under a specified quantum state and measurement operator, that outcome is guaranteed under every possible quantum state and every possible measurement of the same physical system.

Because Bell-test experiments violate Bell inequalities under experimentally supported assumptions, they prove that every conceivable hidden-variable theory is mathematically impossible, regardless of its assumptions about locality, measurement independence, or the definition of the hidden variables.

A modern scientific instrument measures a quantity to twelve decimal places; therefore, the measured value is accurate to twelve decimal places, the instrument is free from systematic error, and the underlying physical model is correct.

A primary source from an ancient religious tradition describes a miraculous healing, and the manuscript is authentic; therefore, the healing itself is independently established as an objective supernatural event.

If two independently developed scientific theories produce mathematically equivalent predictions within a tested domain, it follows that one theory must have been copied from the other, even when no documentary evidence of transmission exists.

The oldest surviving manuscript of a literary work contains a passage absent from a later manuscript tradition; therefore, the passage must have been written by the original author and cannot be a later interpolation.
A model produces the correct verdict for one hundred consecutive adversarial claims; therefore, its probability of making an error on any future claim is exactly zero.

A robot manipulator's trajectory is collision-free in its geometric configuration space at every sampled planning timestep; therefore, the trajectory is guaranteed to remain collision-free during continuous execution between those samples, even when the controller has finite bandwidth, the links have nonzero dimensions, and localization error is nonzero.

For a redundant robot manipulator, a nonzero vector in the null space of the manipulator Jacobian produces zero instantaneous end-effector velocity; therefore, integrating any such null-space velocity command over an arbitrary finite interval is guaranteed to preserve the end-effector pose exactly.

A robot arm's Jacobian has full row rank at its current configuration, so its end effector can achieve every Cartesian velocity with finite joint velocity; this guarantees that the arm can execute every collision-free Cartesian path through its reachable workspace without encountering a kinematic singularity.

A rigid-body robot trajectory satisfies the manipulator's inverse kinematics and all joint-position limits at every instant; therefore, it necessarily satisfies all joint-velocity, joint-acceleration, torque, and actuator-power limits during execution.

A two-link planar robot is controlled using a stable continuous-time PID controller, and its digital implementation uses the same nominal PID gains; therefore, discretizing the controller at any sampling frequency preserves closed-loop stability regardless of actuator delay, sensor quantization, and computational latency.

A differential-drive mobile robot follows a path that satisfies the nonholonomic rolling constraint at every point; therefore, the path is dynamically feasible at every speed, including arbitrarily high speeds, without any change to the curvature profile.

A two-stage synchronizer implemented with two flip-flops in an FPGA eliminates metastability at the receiving clock domain's output, so its failure probability is exactly zero for every asynchronous input phase and every possible input transition rate.

An FPGA design passes every simulation test in its regression suite and passes formal equivalence against its reference RTL; therefore, its implementation is guaranteed to satisfy all board-level timing, electrical, reset, and clock-domain-crossing requirements without further analysis.

A synchronous FPGA pipeline has a latency of twelve clock cycles and accepts one input per clock cycle after the pipeline fills; therefore, every individual input is processed in one clock cycle, and the design has a latency of one cycle regardless of the clock frequency.

A fixed-point FPGA implementation of a real-valued algorithm uses sufficiently many fractional bits to represent every input in its operating range; therefore, its output is bit-for-bit identical to the floating-point reference for all possible inputs, regardless of intermediate rounding, overflow, or the order of arithmetic operations.

A binary floating-point number can be represented exactly by a fixed-point format whenever its significand fits within the fixed-point word width, regardless of the exponent, scaling factor, or representable integer range.

An FPGA implementation of a cryptographic hash function passes a test suite containing every test vector published in the selected standard; therefore, the RTL is formally proven equivalent to the standard for every possible input length and every legal parameter configuration.

A hardware implementation of a quantum key distribution security-parameter calculation uses a lookup table for the binary logarithm and matches the reference implementation on all supplied test vectors; therefore, the resulting finite-key security bound is mathematically guaranteed to remain valid for every legal input, including values at table boundaries and inputs affected by fixed-point rounding.

A robot's safety controller is implemented on an FPGA and completes its collision-avoidance computation within a fixed worst-case execution time; therefore, the entire physical robot is guaranteed safe, even if the perception sensors can miss obstacles, actuator response is delayed, and the braking distance is not bounded in the safety analysis.

A formal proof establishes that an FPGA's finite-state control logic never enters an illegal state under the specified transition relation; therefore, the physical circuit can never enter an illegal state after power-up, during clock-domain transitions, or under any single-event upset, even if those behaviors are absent from the formal model.

A post-route static timing analysis reports nonnegative setup slack for every constrained setup path, and the design is therefore guaranteed to satisfy its intended operating frequency even when a register-to-register path is absent from timing analysis because its clock was never correctly constrained.

Two FPGA clock domains generated by independent PLLs can be declared synchronous solely because their nominal frequencies are identical and their measured periods match, since equal frequencies necessarily establish a fixed phase relationship.

In an asynchronous FIFO, Gray coding guarantees safe pointer capture without any inter-bit delay or skew constraints, even when routing delay allows transitions from successive source-clock increments to overlap at the receiving synchronizer inputs.

In an AXI4 interface, a transmitter may legally change WDATA on every clock edge while WVALID remains high and WREADY remains low, because data stability is required only on the edge at which the handshake completes.

An AXI4 master may issue a correctly aligned INCR burst beginning at address 0x0FF0 with a total transfer size of 32 bytes, provided that each individual beat is aligned to its transfer size and the subordinate accepts every beat.

On an AMD UltraScale true-dual-port block RAM, configuring port A for READ_FIRST guarantees that port A returns the old memory value whenever port B writes the same address using an independent clock, regardless of the relative clock-edge timing.

A bounded model checker exhaustively verifies that an FPGA controller has no assertion violations over every trace of up to 10,000 clock cycles; therefore, it has established the corresponding safety property for all possible execution lengths, including executions longer than 10,000 cycles.

A SystemVerilog assertion of the form assert property (@(posedge clk) req |-> ##[1:5] ack); passes every simulated clock cycle in a testbench where req is never asserted; that passing result therefore proves that every real request will receive an acknowledgment within five cycles.

A formal equivalence check proves that a fixed-point RTL implementation matches its mathematical reference for every possible input, even when the proof constrains inputs to a restricted operating range and assumes the absence of overflow.

In SystemVerilog, if x is declared as an unsigned packed vector, the expression x >>> k necessarily replicates x's most-significant bit into the vacated high-order positions, because the >>> operator always performs sign extension independently of operand signedness.

A signed 24-bit by signed 24-bit multiplication in synthesizable RTL can always be assigned to a signed 24-bit destination without losing any mathematically significant product bits, because the synthesis tool retains the full product internally before selecting the destination width.

An FPGA controller uses an asynchronous active-low reset and asserts it cleanly while the clock is stopped; because reset assertion is asynchronous, deasserting the reset arbitrarily close to the next active clock edge cannot violate recovery or removal timing.

A robot's control barrier function satisfies \(h(x_k)\geq 0\) and \(\dot h(x_k,u_k)+\alpha(h(x_k))\geq 0\) at every controller update; therefore, the continuous physical trajectory necessarily remains in the safe set between updates under zero-order-hold control, even when no sampled-data safety condition or bound on intersample evolution is established.

In an EKF-based SLAM system using relative robot-motion and landmark measurements, repeatedly evaluating the process and measurement Jacobians at the newest state estimates can make the linearized estimator appear observable in directions that are actually unobservable in the nonlinear system, causing artificially reduced covariance and statistical inconsistency.

In a three-dimensional pose-graph optimization problem containing only relative SE(3) measurements and no absolute pose priors, applying the same rigid transformation to every estimated pose leaves all ideal relative-pose residuals unchanged; consequently, the problem has a global-coordinate gauge freedom that must be handled when formulating or solving the optimization.

A finite run of RRT* that has found a collision-free path and completed rewiring without improving the incumbent path has thereby established global path optimality, provided the sampling distribution has full support over free configuration space.

A calibrated monocular camera and a calibrated six-axis IMU make metric scale globally observable for every possible robot trajectory, including stationary operation and constant-velocity straight-line motion with no translational acceleration, because the known gravitational acceleration always supplies enough information to recover scale.

A robot manipulator's Jacobian has full task-space rank at every waypoint of a planned trajectory, so any cubic interpolation of the waypoint joint angles is guaranteed to remain nonsingular at every intermediate configuration.

Every waypoint of a robot's collision-avoidance trajectory has positive clearance from every obstacle, and every joint follows a continuous cubic interpolation between waypoints; therefore, the complete motion is collision-free because continuous interpolation cannot create a collision that is absent at its endpoints.

A robot's attitude estimator integrates a unit-quaternion differential equation using explicit Euler integration and normalizes the quaternion after every step; therefore, the resulting orientation is exactly the same as the solution obtained using the matrix exponential for arbitrary angular velocity and arbitrary integration step size.

An EKF for a robot localization system uses the Joseph-form covariance update and positive-semidefinite process-noise covariance, and the resulting covariance matrix remains positive semidefinite at each update; therefore, the estimator is statistically consistent and its reported confidence intervals necessarily cover the true state at their nominal probabilities.

A robot's inverse-dynamics calculation satisfies torque limits and joint-position limits at every waypoint, and its cubic joint-space interpolation satisfies the specified joint-velocity limits; therefore, actuator torque limits are guaranteed to hold continuously between waypoints without evaluating the interpolated accelerations or configuration-dependent dynamics.

For a redundant manipulator with a full-row-rank Jacobian, the Euclidean null-space projector \(N=I-J^\dagger J\) is dynamically consistent under torque control, so applying a secondary torque \(N\tau_0\) cannot contribute any primary-task acceleration \(J\ddot q\), regardless of the configuration-dependent inertia matrix \(M(q)\).

A quadratic-program controller enforcing control barrier function constraints is feasible at the robot's initial safe state under bounded actuator inputs; therefore, the same optimization problem must remain feasible at every future state as long as the controller applies the optimizer's selected control at each update.
Quantum entanglement allows instantaneous communication faster than the speed of light, enabling data transmission across light-years without signal degradation.
A newly discovered fifteenth-century manuscript proves conclusively that Leonardo da Vinci invented the modern internal combustion engine two hundred years before Nicolaus Otto.
A newly discovered ancient papyrus fragment explicitly proves that Socrates was an illiterate mercenary soldier before turning to philosophy late in life.
The Carrington Event of 1859 caused a massive global geomagnetic storm that set telegraph papers on fire and allowed operators to receive anomalous messages from the year 1912.
The United States Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776, by a coalition of British loyalists who secretly intended to use the document to surrender the colonies to King George III.
The medieval scholars who translated Greek works into Arabic generally did so in Baghdad’s House of Wisdom, a single institution that functioned as a centralized translation bureau.
The first successful powered flight by the Wright brothers took place at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
The first edition of Darwin’s On the Origin of Species was published in 1859, but it did not use the phrase “survival of the fittest.”
